title: S235 later notes: guard the watchdog against a sleep detector never started, and test that the daemon starts it
lead: *Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-09 at HEAD 4707be4. Size S recommended. Status: READY (no decided record conflicts; the S235 later-note leaves the guard form to the owner, see Q1).
findings_note: From the S235 review and gate (2026-11-03), both later: (1) The daemon builds its sleep detector (Wake) once and starts it in recoverRuns. If the start is ever missed, only the watchdog's 30s tick samples the clock (internal/engine/watchdog.go:27). That equals the 30s sleep threshold (internal/engine/wake.go:25), so a tick that arrives slightly late counts 25s as sleep and a silent role could take hours to be killed. PLAUSIBLE: traced by reading, not run. Production starts it today (internal/daemon/runs.go:210). Fix: give the threshold a margin over the tick, for example 2 minutes, or count sleep only after Start has run. (2) No test fails if the Wake Start call at internal/daemon/runs.go:210 is removed; TestStatusCarriesWorkingForARunningRun checks only that both projects share one detector (internal/daemon/runs_test.go:2466). Human checks marked later at approval: a real 35+ minute sleep during a run (no hung pause, status shows slept), and the working line at 100 columns on a live run.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- Source: S235 review and gate, 2026-11-03 (S259 findings). Marked PLAUSIBLE by the author: traced by reading, not run. This spec's first test proves or disproves it.
- Code at HEAD: `Wake.Slept()` samples the clock on every call (`internal/engine/wake.go:91-100`). `sample` adds `gap - every` when `gap > wakeGap` (`wake.go:79-87`). `wakeGap` is 30 s and `wakeSampleEvery` is 5 s (`wake.go:19-25`).
- The background sampler runs only after `Start` (`wake.go:56-73`). The daemon builds the Wake in `initRunManager` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:186-193`) and starts it in `recoverRuns` (`runs.go:227`).
- The watchdog looks every `min(limit/4, 30s)` (`internal/engine/watchdog.go:27`, `:101`) and each look calls `Slept()` through `silence()` (`watchdog.go:91-95`). With a 30 minute limit the look interval is exactly 30 s, equal to `wakeGap`. Without the 5 s sampler, a look that arrives a little late sees `gap > 30s` and counts 25 s as sleep. Silence then grows by about 5 s per look instead of 30 s, so a hung role could live for hours. (Reasoning from the code, not run.)
- No test fails if `d.runs.deps.Wake.Start(ctx)` is removed from `recoverRuns`. `TestStatusCarriesWorkingForARunningRun` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go:2788`) only checks the two projects share one Wake (`:2795`).
- Overlap: `slicer find "Wake"` finds only S235 (done) and S236 (reap process tree, a different problem). Slicer has nothing on this.

### Open questions

1. Which guard? Options: (a) count sleep only after `Start` (recommended: the finding's second form; a never-started Wake can only be wrong, so it counts nothing and the watchdog is exact); (b) raise `wakeGap` to 2 minutes, above the 30 s tick (the finding's first form; it still misjudges if the tick is ever longer); (c) both. Key: `watchdog.wake-guard`.
2. Add a public `Started()` accessor just for the test? Options: (a) yes (recommended, read-only); (b) test through the status `working.slept` of a run after a faked jump. Key: `test.wake-started`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestUnstartedWakeDoesNotHideAHang` (`internal/engine/watchdog_test.go`, beside `hungHarness`): `Deps.Wake = NewWake(clock.Now)` with no `Start`; a fake clock steps 30 s plus 1 ms between watchdog looks; the role is silent. Assert the watchdog kills it at the limit (reason `hung: no output for`), not hours later. Fails first with the current code (slept accumulates 25 s per look).
- `TestWakeCountsASleepOnlyAfterStart` (only for Q1 option a): `NewWake` without `Start`, a 2 hour clock jump, `Slept()` returns 0; after `Start` the same jump counts. The existing `TestWakeCountsAWallClockJumpAsSleep` and `TestWakeSampleIsSynchronous` (`wake_test.go:41`, `:69`) call `Slept()` without `Start`; they then start the Wake first (or use the test constructor).
- `TestWakeThresholdExceedsTheWatchdogTick` (only for Q1 option b): `wakeGap > maxHungCheck` as a compile-time or test assertion, with a margin of at least 90 s.
- `TestRecoverRunsStartsTheWake` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`): after `d.recoverRuns(ctx)` the shared Wake reports started (needs a read-only `Wake.Started() bool`, *proposed*); after cancelling ctx the sampler ends. Assert it fails when the Start call at `runs.go:227` is deleted (mutation check by hand, record it in the report).
- `TestNilWakeStillCountsNothing`: unchanged (`wake_test.go:78`).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Pick the guard from Q1 and add it in `wake.go` only.
2. Add `Started()` (read-only, nil-safe).
3. Add the tests above; confirm the first one fails before the guard.
4. Do not change the 30 minute limit (owner 2026-10-29, `docs/design.md:770`), the working snapshot, or `recoverRuns` order.

Owner decisions (2026-11-09, accepted the recommended answers): Which guard? -> (a) count sleep only after `Start` (recommended: the finding's second form; a never-started Wake can only be wrong, so it counts nothing and the watchdog is exact) [watchdog.wake-guard, adj 199]. Add a public `Started()` accessor just for the test? -> (a) yes (recommended, read-only) [test.wake-started, adj 200].
